items.title: Stormwater Management Master Plan - Preliminary Preferred
notes: Alternative

Report from R. Maiden, Water and Wastewater Capital Project Manager R. Maiden, Project Manager indicated the purpose is to present the preliminary preferred alternatives for the Storm Water Master Plan. He provided background on the project and introduced Matt Senior & Ron Scheckenberger, WSP Global Inc.

Matt Senior & Ron Scheckenberger provided an overview of the study, reported the summary of findings, outlined the alternative assessment and preferred approach, the recommended storm sewer upgrades and financing strategy and the next steps in the process. They noted confirmation of the preferred alternative and approval of the Notice of Study Completion will be presented at the April 29th Council meeting.

The consultants and staff responded to questions on the overall ranking of the options, opportunities for swim ponds, enhancing habitat and biodiversity, use of development manual/guidelines for design, utility user fees and credits, and potential use of wet ponds for firefighting.

items.title: Zoning Amendment RZ015/22 Decision Report - 961 St. David St. N.
notes: Report from M. Iglesias, Manager of Planning Services

M. Iglesias, Manager of Planning Services indicated the property is a 1.4 hectare (3.4 acre) site, on the west side of St. David Street North (Hwy 6), mid-way between Sideroad 19 and 18 in the Fergus Urban Centre, currently containing a residential dwelling and outbuildings to be removed. She indicated the property is designated “Residential” in the Official Plan and adjacent to the “Highway Commercial” designation to the north, noting the purpose of the zoning amendment is to change the zoning from R1A residential exception to higher density residential zones, facilitating an infill development of 49 residential units.

M. Iglesias noted a public meeting was held on August 30, 2023 with concerns raised by neighbours related to potential traffic, noise, wildlife and vegetation impacts, and compatibility. She noted most of the concerns raised have been addressed through recommendations in the technical studies and will become conditions of draft approval of the plan of condominium. In addition, other matters such as detailed grading/drainage, tree removals, landscaping, fencing and noise mitigation measures will be addressed through a future detailed design.
M. Iglesias indicated staff is recommending approval of the zoning amendment to facilitate a 49 unit infill residential development proposal
